correction_scope: Versioned semantic and accounting correction for the inherited v0.17 baseline locator of Telecom Egypt RDH2 Smart Village Campus (Regional Data Hub 2). The selected OSM polygon is the whole Smart Village business park; it was labelled and counted as a campus locator. The numeric polygon, display anchor, raw capture hash, physical site, project, identity and commissioning observation are unchanged. The entity kind, use scope, method, scope class, precision and uncertainty statements, evidence key and verification posture are corrected to host-development locality context. No added or removed campus or project, lifecycle refresh, finer location, boundary, precision gain or acceptance claim.

supersedes.correction_reason: The v0.16 seven-country batch turned a locality-only statement (Smart Village, Giza; curated method authoritative_locality with null coordinates and geometry) into the whole named OSM Smart Village polygon and labelled it geometry_use_scope campus_locator, although its own precision scope calls it the broad host development. v0.17 and every v0.18 draft therefore count RDH2 as a reviewed site locator and publish the planar centroid of the business park's longitude/latitude ring as its latitude and longitude. The polygon is about 382.32 ha, roughly 1,000 times the 3,825 m2 land area the contractor reports for RDH2; it contains 88 mapped buildings, 38 of them named for many other organisations and for separate Telecom Egypt and TE Data buildings, and Telecom Egypt's own releases place its RDH data-centre phases, including RDH phase 1 launched in Q1 2021, in Smart Village. No reviewed source places RDH2 at any position within it. It intersects no other selected site.

defect_findings.finding: The selected geometry is the whole Smart Village business park (OSM way 545580264 v6; 12 distinct vertices in a closed way of 13 node references; about 382.32 ha WGS84 geodesic; bounding box about 2.69 km by 2.72 km), labelled geometry_use_scope campus_locator and entity kind campus. The v0.16 record's own precision scope calls it 'the broad host development'. The RDH2 source supports locality only (curated method authoritative_locality, null coordinates and geometry, address 'Smart Village, Giza, Egypt'). Smart Villages Development and Management Company describes the park as Egypt's largest gated business community, with 2.5 million m2 of land, 94 operating buildings and 244 business partners.

Project and site latitude/longitude publish the planar centroid of the business park's longitude/latitude ring (31.021793794673577, 30.07671059884446; the v0.16 record labels it planar_polygon_centroid), a host-development centroid with spurious precision. Polygon vertices lie up to 1.388 km away, and the nearest mapped building outline to it is HSBC Bank's (OSM way 336802979), about 17 m away; the anchor lies inside no mapped building.
ECG's captured RDH2 project page (2026-07-21, sha256 6d7c0708...) reports a 3,825 m2 land area and 2,300 m2 built area; the polygon is roughly 1,000 times that land area.

In the 2026-10-08 OSM snapshot 88 buildings lie wholly inside the polygon, 38 of them named for other organisations and units (Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, Huawei, Ericsson, HSBC, NTRA, the communications ministry and others), including a separate Telecom Egypt office building (way 270809613) and a TE Data building (way 293130215) that are alias hazards. Telecom Egypt press release 132 (2020) places its then-new international data centre, due for commissioning in early 2021, in Smart Village among many other companies and authorities; press release 188 (2023) says RDH's first phase launched in Q1 2021, makes RDH2 its second phase and plans two further phases 'within the Smart Village availability zone'. The polygon therefore cannot distinguish RDH2 from RDH1, future RDH phases or other tenants.
Unlike CGK, the polygon intersects no other selected site geometry, and RDH2 is the only Egypt site among the 200. The defect is scope and accounting, not a demonstrated collision.

RDH2 is counted in reviewed_site_locator_projects (197 at the thirty-sixth checkpoint) with posture recent_authoritative_physical_observation_plus_reviewed_site_locator. Under the CGK rule a host-development polygon is not a reviewed site locator; the v0.18 docstring states that locality centroids are excluded.

The numbers are a faithful copy: canonical geometry 343 bytes, sha256 818708ea..., reproduced from the 2026-10-08 Geofabrik free GeoPackage after unwrapping its single-part MultiPolygon and reversing the vertex order. OSM node coordinates are WGS84, so this is a scope, selection and accounting error, not a datum or transcription error.

Frozen in v0.17 (projects.csv line 97, sites.csv line 93, evidence.csv line 88, sites.geojson feature 91) and copied byte for byte into every v0.18 draft through the thirty-sixth. The v2 baseline-correction path added for CGK can correct it without a further builder extension.
